notes.title: Version 0.632 + August Developer Update
notes.content:
This update includes new cutscenes for major townsfolk quests and some additional visual adjustments and fixes.

Read below the patch notes for a quick developer update!

[h1]Version 0.632 Patch Notes[/h1]
[h2]Gameplay Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added cutscenes for Returning to Roots 1 (Alimela) and Magnum Opus 1 (Zoji)
[/list]

[h2]Visual Updates[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fog effects updated - will now change based on time of day and season
[*] Fixed an issue where the tavern bar appears black
[*] Replaced a missing door in the Carpenter building
[*] Minor terrain texture updates
[*] Collision added back to the path edges around town
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed the type name widget not scaling properly when using a controller in the sign-up process
[*] Fixed issue with login buttons not properly fading and showing on Steam Deck resolution
[*] Fixed issue with prompts not changing to controller buttons from PC button
[/list]

[h2]August Developer Update[/h2]

It's about time for a quick Developer Update on what we've been up to lately! 

Just last week, we greatly streamlined the account creation and sign-in process. There's no longer any need to enter your login email and password - just open the game and you will be able to log in automatically, or create a Spellfarers character much faster if you're a first time player. 

Our team is currently in the process of animating and implementing cutscenes for the major story quests — some of which have already been added to the game. You'll see these when completing personal quests for townsfolk after getting to know them and helping them out. This update brings cutscenes into the first quests for Zoji and Alimela's quest lines, and more are on the way in the near future!

On the gameplay mechanics side of things, we're also nearing completion of a much-needed update to the furniture placement mode! Organizing your home and rearranging your furniture will become much smoother and easier to work with, so your hut can be the cozy home it was always meant to be. 

We've also got a new trailer in the works to show off the game that you'll be able to feast your eyes on soon, so stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107734/a399b7e3bfa85f1eba9be64f36975529037d28fc.png[/img]

[h1]Version 0.600: Camera Updates, Sound Effects, and Bug Fixes![/h1]

Just in time for spring cleaning, today's update has introduced a long-awaited camera system revamp,  finally bringing us to Version 0.600 of Spellfarers! Expect much smoother camera behaviour and better looking dialogue scenes in this release. Walls, stairs, and other terrain will feel a lot better and smoother to navigate on and around. 

We've also added a ton of new sound effects for actions, another ongoing process. The audio for walking on grass also has been touched up, and for those with apiaries at their homestead, the furious buzzing of thousands of bees will be a little more subdued. 

[h2]Version 0.600 Patch Notes[/h2]

[h3]Gameplay Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Camera System! 
[*] Dinner Parties are now functional - invite your coven over and share some good food!
[*] Lots of new sounds! Many homestead, item, and animal interactions (too many to list here) have been given sound to liven up a day of farming, tending to your critters, and crafting.
[*] Adjusted bee buzzing to a level below deafening
[*] Revised grass footstep audio
[/list]
[h3]UI Updates[/h3]
[list]
[*] Updated Credits
[*] Sped up exit from Profile and Inspect Player widgets
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed being unable to stand up after sitting
[*] Fixed possible invalid weather setting
[*] Fixed an issue where visiting guests may be sent to upper town when entering host's hut under certain conditions
[*] Fixed hut items disappearing after having visited a friend
[*] Building interiors now load and unload properly when fast traveling 
[*] Navigation and styling fixes for account Registration
[*] Fixed colour-changeable clothing being too shiny
[/list]

[h1]Developer Update - What's Next?[/h1]

So, what's next now that we're onto 0.600 and beyond? Currently, one of our focuses is working on cutscenes for many dialogue sequences, like the personal quests for the various townsfolk. One of Jinni's quests, Smelted Souvenir, has already had this incorporated in today's update, in fact! More are in the storyboarding and development stage right now and will be making their way into the game over time to give the local townsfolk a chance for their unique personalities and stories to shine.

Beyond that, we've got a big rework of Tile Mode in the future to make decorating your homestead and placing furniture a smoother experience, so you can feel encouraged to get creative with your space and the new items you acquire over time.

Remember to [url=https://discord.com/invite/pHQUtsVkD3]join the Discord[/url] to share your feedback and discuss the latest updates and upcoming changes!

[h1]Developer Update[/h1]

Hello 2025 - and Year of the Snake!

It's the first Developer Update of the new year and we've been back at full development pace on Spellfarers for a little while, having recently welcomed an additional programmer to the Digital Leisure team! So, here's a quick look at where we are and what's in the works next.

[h3]Amicable Animations[/h3]

One of the current major focuses of development continues to be the NPC animation updates. We've been implementing more animations for the townsfolk, updating pathing and routines, and overall making the residents of Wenngrove more lively and expressive. You'll continue to see more gradual improvements and updates as we smooth out the rough edges and add more animations.

[h3]Controls and Camera[/h3]

Full controller support is another thing that will be ready soon, with the addition of an on-screen keyboard and more functionality. This also means better compatibility for Steam Deck players.

We've also been planning out a revamp of the camera system which will reduce clipping, improve dialogue scenes, and overall make the camera much smoother.

[h3]...And More[/h3]

More starting character customization options are also in the works, and we're updating the default player avatar templates for new players to work from to make use of them.

We're approaching a milestone version number in the near future! Thanks for playing, Witches, and we'll be back with another Developer Update with Version 0.600!

[h1]Spellfarers Developer Update - December 2024[/h1]

The year is coming to a close, so it's time for one more Spellfarers Developer Update!
If you haven't checked in on Spellfarers development in a while, here's a quick update on some of the larger feature updates:

-Revamped progression and homestead upgrades
-Backpack and Tool Belt upgrades
-Fishing rework
-Much, much more

We've had some more major updates lately between updates to fishing, progression, and land expansion; including this week's Tool Belt addition and mining/treecutting changes. We're now comfortably approaching the end of Phase 1 on our development roadmap: 
https://steamcommunity.com/app/1569420/discussions/0/4522261213601974336/


Minor economy updates are always possible in the future, but we're pretty happy with the overall state of the in-game economy at present. There are still some additional things in the works for the Phase 1 component of storage upgrades and expansions, but soon enough we'll be moving onto Phase 2: Fun and Functionality.

Phase 2 will make things feel a lot livelier in the town of Wenngrove, adding much more animation to the residents and their daily schedules, polish, a new character in Hannan, and more. We'll also focus more on iterating and polishing the menu and UI systems during this time to achieve full controller support in addition to mouse and keyboard.

The pace of updates will naturally slow down later into December as the holiday season approaches, but we're not done for the year just yet!

Thanks for continuing to follow along during our Early Access development! We look forward to making even bigger strides in the new year and working towards the Spellfarers 1.0 release in 2025.

[h1]October Developer Update[/h1]

It's every Witch's favourite season! We're now over two months into Early Access and we have a brief developer update on what we're doing and where we're headed. The update pace is a little less breakneck than the past days of early access lately, but lots of work is continuing behind the scenes and the team has been expanding!

Lately, we've been making adjustments to the early experience based on your feedback, with new early game quests and other features to help players become familiar with the Minor Transmutation Spell once they've unlocked it and learn what kind of materials it can be used to create. Most items now have their descriptions properly implemented, which will ease the learning curve - some spell descriptions still to come in the near future.

We've also introduced some UI improvements that should make it clear how much progress has been made on harvesting resource nodes. As of last week's update, progress bars now appear when mining or chopping trees to nearby players so you can see your progress and make it easier to join in and work together with fellow Witches.

In the very near future, we are continuing an ongoing overhaul of the menu systems, standardizing their layouts and improving visuals and polish. We'll also be refining the new features above, so we'd love to hear your impressions on them!

Looking ahead, we have plans to make upgrades more available and visible, so that players have additional direction via items, quests, and dialogue to help them actually learn about and reach new and existing upgrades. notes.title: Developer Update: Pest Control and Version 0.514 Patch Notes
notes.content:
This update includes many adjustments to quests, and should ease the requirements of early-game quests as well as properly gate later-game quests until you can obtain the required items.

[h1]Developer Update - Pest Control [/h1]

It’s been a whirlwind here at the office the last few weeks. Early Access has been live for 14 business days, and we’ve released just as many patches. Whew!

 While we’re swatting down bugs as fast as possible, we wanted to give you an update on what’s going on at the office with regards to some of our longer-term targets. (Given that we’re patching daily so far, “longer term” in this case means hopefully within the next few weeks.)

[olist]
[*][b]Quests and balancing are still top of mind for us.[/b]

We’ve finished a first pass at re-jigging some of the requirements to get a noticeboard quest. A lot of early-game noticeboard quests will have their turn-in requirements reduced and should be easier to complete. Many later-game quests have been pushed further out, so you shouldn’t get those quests until you have the ability to make or get the required items.
Following this, we are planning to adjust reward values to better reflect item costs, and make the quests available more often. This does mean that favor values will be adjusted down, but given the increased availability of quests, this should mean it won’t hurt as much to turn down a quest you don’t want to do, and overall make it easier to earn favor.

[*][b]We’ve heard your storage woes, and will work on making more storage available more quickly.[/b]

Ah, the bane of every RPG – the inventory management game. While we do have options for expanding storage in a variety of ways, literally all of them are too harshly gated. We’ll be adjusting those down in the near future to make it easier to store your stuff. This is slated for review early next week, and will take some time to implement.

[*]  [b]Controls and Accessibility passes to make it easier for everyone to play.[/b]

We really appreciate your feedback on this one. Camera controls, fishing, and being able to hold instead of tapping buttons for harvesting trees etc. are top of our list in this category. Adjustments to these items will be ongoing, as it affects a variety of interfaces, and will therefore take some time. But it is a priority for us that everyone can play in a way that is comfortable for them.
Thank you again, as always, to our players for your reports and feedback! With your help, we will keep building, bug swatting, and making things better!
[/olist]


[h1]Version 0.514 Update Notes[/h1]

[h2]Gameplay Updates[/h2]

[*] Made many early quests easier
[*] Gated many later-game quests until prerequisite items can be obtained
[/list]

[h2]Developer Update - One Week of Early Access![/h2]

One of the common points of feedback we've read is with respect to shards and progression. We wanted to provide a quick developer update touching on these concerns and our plans going forward regarding this, as well as how later stages of the game will affect this. Some issues are being addressed now, others are in consideration for future improvements.

[olist]
[*][b]Some players are getting stuck on quests that are either too expensive, or buggy. This impacts progression, and players aren't getting the shards that we had expected. (Fireflies, straw bales, etc.)[/b]

In the short term, we are fixing affected quests (such as the Ilo fix in this patch). Harder quests will be moved further down the progression line as needed.
In the long term, we will be making more daily quests that are easier to do. Where possible these should be instructive, showing you more about what the game has to do in the early game.

[*][b]Some players are using their shards at the apothecary a lot more than anticipated, resulting in faster shard usage than expected.[/b]

Currently, transmuting the reagents you need should be the answer more often than not. If there is a case where purchasing from Zoji is a cheaper solution, let us know. We may need to communicate better that we view Zoji as a vendor to be used for a few purchases once in a while for most people to fill out some missing ingredients.
	
[*][b]As the days go on, players will start to approach larger milestones with their favour such as apprenticeship. Here is how things will eventually play out once you eventually reach those longer-term milestones and how that will help with shard costs.[/b]

Once you reach enough favour with someone, you can choose to apprentice for them. You will only be able to apprentice for one trade at a time. That person will then ask you to do a larger, more time-consuming and costly quest; such as transmuting 15 Peonies. However, these quests will unlock additional rewards like the ability to purchase Peonies for Gold. This will be the case for most of your growable/fishable/forageable items.	
	
Getting more easy early quests should ease the pains of shard costs and early progression. Gold will later be a much more useful resource, once you can use it to purchase the next tier of items.

We expect a lot of discussion around this and we appreciate all the feedback so far! We hope you all will feel like you are making more informed decisions with your shards, knowing more of how things will progress.
	
[*][b]Wilds foraging. Stone is currently the go-to method for gold.[/b]

The merchants have received enough stone by now, so we're nerfing gold for stone. Sorry. But also, more plots! All players will begin with 24 maximum plots to play with going forward. Further down the line we want to give you more things to do to earn your gold (and favour) particularly in the early game - which we are all still in!
[/olist]

Spellfarers is a week into Early Access and it has been an extremely helpful week! Thank you for sharing your feedback and your experience with this game and we can't wait to continue building and improving Spellfarers!

[h2]Early Access Starts Now![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107734/2eaf8b0690c745deb9e36e3483b2c89303e94e70.jpg[/img]

Farm, fish, craft, and cast spells with your friends in this idyllic, magical multiplayer Farming Sim - available now in Early Access! Journey to the town of Wenngrove, meet the townsfolk, and summon your trusty Familiar to help guide you. 

This is the Version 0.500 release of the game and it is an evolving experience, with many game aspects subject to change. Thanks to Early Access, we plan to continue development of the game and act on player feedback to create the ideal cozy Spellfarers experience. If you want to play a more polished, full experience of Spellfarers, we would encourage you to wishlist the game and wait for our official release, planned for Q1 2025.

[h3]What is currently in the game?[/h3]

Currently in Spellfarers, you can grow and gather ingredients, cast spells, build decorations, clothing, and items. You can interact with the townsfolk of Wenngrove, as well as other player-controlled Witches in town. You’ll have your own private Witch Hut to decorate as you like, and a Familiar to keep you company as you explore the town. There are a number of quests to complete and magic spells to learn, with more to come!

See the [url=https://spellfarers.com/]Spellfarers website[/url] for more details, character profiles, and Frequently Asked Questions!
